text: A pro soccer player just died after this collision. Here's how a hit like this can kill.
Jesús de Miguel, thirty, played forward for Tenerife in Spain.
On Monday night, deep in stoppage time, he chased a long ball.
Andorra's keeper rushed out, and his knee caught him in the chest. The impact also hit his head.
A hit like this can kill in two ways.
First, the chest. A hard blow at just the wrong moment of a heartbeat can knock the heart out of rhythm.
Instead of pumping, it just quivers. Without CPR and a shock from a defibrillator within minutes, the brain runs out of oxygen.
Second, the head. The brain slams against the inside of the skull, and it can bleed and swell.
The skull can't stretch, so the pressure builds and squeezes the brain, sometimes hours later.
He went down and didn't move. The keeper got a red card, and the match was called off.
Reports say his heart stopped on the way to the hospital, and paramedics got it going again.
At first he was stable. Then his club said his condition got worse, and on Tuesday he died. No official cause has been released.
If a player goes down and doesn't move, call for help, start CPR, and get the defibrillator.
Rest in peace, Jesús de Miguel.
